items: **Days to harvest:** 50 to 65 days from sowing to the first harvest.
**Yield:** 10 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: Key facts about Kentucky snap bean
How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Kentucky snap bean takes 50 to 65 days from sowing to the first harvest. That is 3.3 days longer than the average of the 8 pole snap bean varieties with a day count, 54.2 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 10 t/ha trails the average of its group, 14. It sits in the lower quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?
No pest or disease ratings are published for this variety. So treat it as untested, and scout every week.

The pests and diseases that hit snap bean fields most often: [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [cutworm](/pests/cutworm), [leafminer](/pests/leafminer), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant Kentucky snap bean

Baguio beans like cool weather, so most come from the highlands of Benguet and Mountain Province. Pole types bear longer, and bush types fit a short cropping gap. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Vegetables in the Philippines](/crops/vegetables-philippines).

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes 50 to 65 days from sowing to the first harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 10 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Kentucky?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
